items.title: Rewrites 500 on GET/HEAD requests that carry a body: "Request with a GET or HEAD method cannot have a body"

labels.name: - P3: minor bug
labels.description: An edge case that only affects very specific usage (priority)

items.body:
### Astro Info

```
Astro: 6.4.2
Adapter: @astrojs/cloudflare 13.6.0 (bug is adapter-independent; any runtime that delivers a GET with a body triggers it)
```

### Describe the Bug

`copyRequest()` in `packages/astro/src/core/routing/rewrite.ts` forwards `body: oldRequest.body` unconditionally when cloning the incoming request for a rewrite. If the incoming request is a GET/HEAD that carries a body, `new Request()` throws per the Fetch spec:

```
TypeError: Request with a GET or HEAD method cannot have a body.
    at createRequest (…)
    at copyRequest (…)
    at applyRewriteToState (…)
    at Rewrites.execute (…)
    at async Object.rewrite (…)
```

The throw happens inside the rewrite machinery (not user code), so every `Astro.rewrite()` / `next('/404')` on such a request becomes a 500.

GET-with-body sounds exotic, but it happens in production: the **Facebook iOS in-app browser** (FBAN/FBIOS UA) sends GET requests with a body when retrying image loads. On our site, its retry loops on a dead image URL (~100 req/min bursts) turned every not-found rewrite into a 500 and paged our monitoring — while the app's own not-found handling would have served a 404. Nothing in userland can catch it: the throw is between the route's `Astro.rewrite("/404")` call and the target render.

Constructor-created `Request`s can never carry a GET body (the constructor is exactly what throws), but runtime-delivered ones can — Cloudflare's workerd hands them to the app as-is, and Node servers accept GET bodies too.

### What's the expected result?

Rewrites succeed; the body is dropped for methods that forbid one. Suggested guard in `copyRequest`:

```ts
const forbidsBody = oldRequest.method === "GET" || oldRequest.method === "HEAD";
// …
body: forbidsBody ? null : oldRequest.body,
```

### Link to Minimal Reproducible Example

Runtime-specific (constructor-created requests can't reproduce it), so steps instead of a StackBlitz:

1. `npm create astro` → SSR with `@astrojs/cloudflare`, a catch-all `[...slug].astro` that does `return Astro.rewrite("/404")`.
2. `astro build && wrangler dev` on the built worker.
3. `curl -X GET --data x http://localhost:8787/anything-missing` → 500 + the TypeError above in the logs. Without `--data`: 404.

Happy to turn the suggested guard into a PR if that helps.
